definition: The increase in an amount written as a percentage of the original amount: $\frac{\text{increase}}{\text{original}} \times 100$. Increases and decreases are both percentage changes.
The decrease in an amount written as a percentage of the original amount: $\frac{\text{decrease}}{\text{original}} \times 100$.
Interest worked out on the principal only, so it is the same every year: $I = \frac{P \times R \times T}{100}$ for a rate of $R\%$ per year over $T$ years.
Interest that is added to the amount each year, so the next year's interest is worked out on the new total; after $n$ years at $r\%$ the value is $P\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^{n}$.
The amount of money first invested or borrowed, before any interest is added.
The difference between the selling price and the cost price: a profit if the item sells for more than it cost, a loss if it sells for less; as a percentage it is compared with the cost price.
Finding the original amount from the amount after a percentage change, by dividing the new amount by the multiplier, such as $54 \div 1.2 = 45$ after a $20\%$ increase.
